Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Issue: Make the six failing queries run on 1 CN (fusion, spill, or both). Three designs were written to /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/fragment-fusion-surgical.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/fragment-fusion-robust.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/fragment-fusion-upstream.md. Their structured summaries: [
 {
  "summary": "Surgical fix for \"six queries cannot run on 1 CN\": CN-only, TPlan-level fusion of single-destination local leaf senders into their receiver. When a leaf sender (no EXCHANGE_NODE of its own) arrives with a DATA_STREAM_SINK that is HASH_PARTITIONED to exactly one destination on this CN, whose registered receiver expects exactly one sender on that exchange and whose exchange node is plain (no sort_info/limit/conjuncts, row_tuples equal, parent not an AGGREGATION_NODE), the CN does not run it: it stores the sender's TExecPlanFragmentParams as a new SenderSource::LocalFused in LocalExchange. When the receiver's sender set completes, the sender's TPlan.nodes are spliced in place of the EXCHANGE_NODE, its scan ranges merged, the exchange removed from per_exch_num_senders, and the fused plan translated/run as one fragment. All six failing fragments are exactly this shape (measured from the dumps: HASH_PARTITIONED, 1 destination, per_exch :1, leaf FILE_SCAN, no output_exprs). No engine, translator, FE, proto or wire change; broadcast senders, merge aggregations and 4-CN behaviour untouched. Full design with code excerpts at /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/fragment-fusion-surgical.md (dump parse in the same directory: parse_dumps.py, all-dumps.txt).",
  "mechanism": "Today: process_fragment (compute_node_service.rs:918-950) registers receivers via register_receiver (local_exchange.rs:105-140) and translates+runs leaf senders (:949); execute_fragment_with_inputs (:1020-1215) runs the sender with run_labeled(\"sender\") (:1175-1187), parking its whole output on the GPU, then push_sender (:1193) records SenderSource::LocalParked; take_ready (local_exchange.rs:248-310) releases the receiver when all senders are complete; execute_ready_fragment (:1325-1385) binds each exchange to a stream view and translate_exchange (node_translator.rs:637-720) lowers it to a stream read. Nothing streams across the boundary (engine.rs:278-280, run_fragment_inner :486-720, sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745), and parked repositories are outside the downgrade sweep (streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112, downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232/294-300), so the lineitem leaf parks 66-104 GB and dies. Change: (1) fragment_fusion.rs (new, pure): fusable_leaf_sender (leaf, DATA_STREAM_SINK, HASH_PARTITIONED, destinations.len()==1, route Local, no limit/output_columns/output_exprs), fusable_receiver_exchange (EXCHANGE_NODE num_children 0, limit -1, no conjuncts, no sort_info, offset 0, row_tuples == sender root row_tuples per ExchangeNode.java:183-186, preorder parent not AGGREGATION_NODE so merge_exchange_overrides node_translator.rs:438-470 stays satisfied), splice_leaf (replace the exchange entry with the sender's preorder node list, merge per_node_scan_ranges and node_to_per_driver_seq_scan_ranges which ScanFilePaths::from_fragment scan_paths.rs:62-90 reads, remove per_exch_num_senders entry; the descriptor table is query-wide so slot refs resolve unchanged). (2) local_exchange.rs: SenderSource::LocalFused{params} (is_complete true), offer_fused_sender(key, sender_id, params) -> Fused(Option<ReadyFragment>) | Declined(reason) under the lock. (3) compute_node_service.rs: try_fuse_leaf_sender called in try_dispatch_sender (:309-331, before queueing) and in process_fragment before translate (:949); execute_ready_fragment partitions ready.inputs into fused (splice into params) and streamed (today's path), dumps the fused params, translates the fused plan; env gate SIRIUS_CN_FUSE_LOCAL_LEAVES (default on) next to async_sender_dispatch (:289-296). Any non-match declines to today's run-and-park, so a wrong guess costs performance not correctness. Under q05: leaves customer(1), orders(4) fuse into F04, lineitem(9) into F08, nation(18) into F14; region/supplier broadcasts park as today; fused F08 = lineitem scan inline JOIN stream 7 (227.6M rows declared exact) JOIN supplier stream; DuckDB's build/probe optimizer (duckdb build_probe_side_optimizer.cpp:160-212, swap rule :185-188; SEMI/ANTI flip :226-240) builds on the smaller side and streams lineitem, the same mechanism that produced q04's RIGHT_SEMI flip in cn1/engine-cn0.log:48480 (Sirius accepts RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI, sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:242-246). Engine runs 11 -> 7; predicted peak < 30 GB vs 104.3 GB parked. Receiver-first arrival is guaranteed by the FE's stage-by-stage deploy (ExecutionDAG.java:169-200, Deployer.java:208-215) and measured (cn1/cluster.log:4142-4202).",

  "predicted_effect": "Inference from measured sizes and the standalone runs. q05: PASS ~3.2-4.0 s warm (standalone 2.79 s), peak < 30 GB vs 104.3 GB parked today. q08: PASS ~4-5 s (standalone 3.67), ~10 GB of broadcast streams parked plus orders/customer hash builds, ~25-35 GB peak. q09: PASS ~6-7.5 s (standalone 5.43) but least headroom: ~31 GB parked (orders 1.5e9 rows ~18 GB, partsupp ~13 GB as broadcasts) plus a 1.5e9-row hash build (standalone shows the same HASH_JOIN(31) in=36.60GB), ~70-90 GB peak, medium confidence. q17: PASS ~7-10 s (standalone 3.79; the FE's partial aggregation over all of lineitem runs first, ~6 s wall, then the fused join fragment scans lineitem again ~3 s), ~20 GB peak. q18: PASS ~4.5-6.5 s (standalone 2.69), 24 GB parked partial-agg + ~36 GB merge state + orders in flight ~ 65 GB. q21: most likely still OOM: fusing l3 and l2 removes 77.76 + 73.5 GB of parking, but DuckDB compares stream 9 (~1.85e9 exact rows) with the l3 scan estimate (6e9 x 0.2 = 1.2e9) and flips the anti join to build on l3, whose actual filtered size is ~3.8e9 rows (~45 GB + hash table) plus ~22 GB parked stream 9 > 100 GiB; passes at ~60-70 GB only if the flip does not happen; with fix 1 the failure costs ~3-5 s instead of 114 s. Coverage 15/22 -> 20/22 (21/22 if q21 passes; q16 is the translator gap). Sweep: the six cost 774.9 s of 910.3 s today; predicted ~180-200 s with fix 1, ~300 s without. Of the 15 passing queries 11 are plan-identical; q02 (4 leaves fuse, 13 -> 9 engine runs), q07 (lineitem 59.5 GB no longer parked, 10 -> 7 runs), q13 (orders 18.2 GB, 5 -> 3), q20 (partsupp ~12 GB, 8 -> 6) lose parking and fixed per-fragment cost (~100-300 ms each, inference). Fused inline scans with conjuncts also become eligible for dynamic filters (sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:646-664), which parked streams never were. 4 CNs: no change by construction.",
  "risks": [
   "Fused leaves plan with DuckDB's parquet estimate x 0.2 per conjunct instead of the exact parked cardinality (C2); a wrong build side is a memory/time regression, never a wrong answer. This is the q21 mechanism; for the four changed passing queries the sides are >= 5x apart so no flip is expected. Mitigation: env gate, A/B arm, per-query fused-count check.",
   "Order dependence: fusion needs the receiver registered before the leaf arrives. Guaranteed by the FE's default stage-by-stage deploy (ExecutionDAG.java:169-200, Deployer.java:208-215) and measured for q05 (cluster.log:4142-4202); under enable_single_node_schedule (DefaultCoordinator.java:697-704, Deployer.java:359-390) RPCs can race and the design then declines to today's behaviour (logged). An order-independent variant (hold the leaf's params under the exchange key, decide at register_receiver) is ~30 more lines if ever needed.",

Covered by the translator-level test.",

CN-only change under experimental/starrocks -> fork PR in the carve plan; no engine (src/) PR, no FE patch, no proto or FE rebuild.",

If the FE keeps lineitem in the join's fragment there is nothing to fuse; if the broadcast memory penalty still routes lineitem through a single-destination shuffle, fusion applies. Fix 3 is the most plausible route to q21 (FE pushing the supplier/nation join below the semi/anti).",

  "summary": "Fuse same-node single-sender exchange edges on the CN before translation: when a sender fragment S has exactly one destination, that destination is local, its receiver R is registered and pending, and R.per_exch_num_senders[E]==1, R records S's thrift params under exchange node E (inheriting S's own exchanges through an instance-id redirect) and, when ready, the translator lowers S's plan in place of the stream read. On 1 CN every exchange is local and single-sender, so a query collapses to 1 + (#merge-fed exchanges) engine runs; the fused plan is re-planned by the engine's DuckDB optimizer (JOIN_ORDER + BUILD_SIDE_PROBE_SIDE enabled at sirius_ffi.cpp:134-138, 233-243), i.e. the standalone shape that already passes all six at 2.7-6.4 s. Rust-only (translator crate + CN), no engine or FE change, one knob SIRIUS_CN_FRAGMENT_FUSION=off|leaf|all (default all), every fuse/skip logged with a reason. Full design with code excerpts: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/fragment-fusion-robust.md",
  "mechanism": "Sender arrival (compute_node_service.rs exec_single_attachment :705-717 and translate_batch_attachment :1646-1676) calls a new ServiceCore::try_fuse before try_dispatch_sender (:309-329): sink must be DATA_STREAM_SINK with one destination routing Local (route_destination :1251-1275), no sink limit/non-identity output_columns, no fragment.output_exprs; then the translator's pure exchange_fusability(receiver, sender, E) refuses merge-fed exchanges (keys of merge_exchange_overrides, node_translator.rs:438-483 — two-phase aggregation boundaries are kept), output_exprs, and a sender-root row_tuples != TExchangeNode.input_row_tuples (FE guarantee ExchangeNode.java:180-185; verified on q05 dumps fragment-0137:3003-3030 vs fragment-0141:11-27, both [6]). LocalExchange::try_fuse_sender (under the existing mutex) resolves the destination through a new absorbed: instance->owner redirect map, requires expected_senders[E]==1, removes E, stores the sender under PendingReceiver.fused[E], moves the sender's own expected exchanges into the receiver, and re-runs take_ready (:248-313) so a receiver emptied by fusion is dispatched through the same FragmentOutcome path a completing sender uses today (:716). push_sender (:142-155) and push_remote_frame (:159-246) resolve through absorbed, so later local senders or remote frames addressed at an absorbed instance complete the owner (safe on multi-CN too). Translation: translate_fragment_with_inputs(params, exchange_inputs, fused) merges ScanFilePaths per query-global scan node id (scan_paths.rs:62-93 + new extend_from_fragment), runs merge_exchange_overrides/common_slots_consumed_above per grafted plan, and translate_exchange (:637-763) translates the grafted TPlan (TranslatePlan for TPlan :164-175), applies confine_carried (:2338-2345) so a carrying root never hits refuse_carried_join_child (:1880-1895), asserts the row layout, then keeps the existing sort_info/apply_conjuncts/apply_fetch handling (merging exchanges keep their SortRel, offset/limit preserved); no StreamInputSchema is pushed for a fused exchange so the engine (engine.rs:508-587) declares only real streams. Build/probe side is decided by DuckDB's BuildProbeSideOptimizer (build_probe_side_optimizer.cpp:160-246), which measured-ly flips the translator's LeftSemi to RIGHT_SEMI on this engine (q04 HASH_JOIN type: RIGHT_SEMI, P5), so q21 does not hard-depend on a translator RIGHT_SEMI arm (added anyway as a 15-line companion for fix 3). Sender-before-receiver arrival falls back to today's park path (logged NoPendingReceiver), so fusion can never hang. Fused-run failures reach the FE via run_ready_fragment -> results.fail_query (:864-911), the same path as intermediate receiver failures today.",

  "predicted_effect": "Measured baseline: the six die after 54-232 s (774.9 s of the 910.3 s 1-CN sweep) with 17,917 OOM-reschedule lines; standalone runs the same SQL in 2786/3674/5427/3786/2691/6401 ms warm, all oracle MATCH. Predicted (inference = standalone warm x the measured 1-CN/standalone parity band 0.95-1.2 for scan-heavy queries): q05 2650-3350 ms, q08 3500-4400, q09 5150-6500, q17 3600-4550, q18 2550-3250, q21 6100-7700 (medium confidence, emulated anti join); engine runs per query drop from 11/11/9/5/7/9 FE fragments to 2/2/2/3/2/2 (one per merge-fed exchange plus one); the parked lineitem projections of 73-245 GB never exist; the six take ~25-30 s of the sweep instead of 775 s. For the 15 passing queries at 1 CN in all mode: fragment-heavy small queries (q02 2.18x, q11 2.88x, q15 1.78x, q22 1.90x of standalone today) move toward standalone as the per-fragment engine windows, receiver-first waits and relays disappear; scan-heavy queries stay within noise; peak pool usage drops by the parked volumes (q07 79.1 GB, q04 30.8 GB, q13 1.48B rows, q20 800M+304M rows, q22 1.5B rows). On 4 CNs fusion rarely triggers (per_exch_num_senders==4, broadcasts have 4 destinations), so plans and timings are unchanged. leaf mode also rescues all six (every failing park is a leaf scan) with fewer plan changes: q05 runs 5 engine fragments instead of 11.",
  "risks": [
   "A fused plan loses the exact declared stream cardinality at former boundaries and relies on DuckDB estimates; C2/BJ-4 measured the FE's IS NOT NULL conjunct getting DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY 0.2 (q10 built on the 25.5 GB side). A previously passing query could plan worse (slower or OOM, which fix 1 bounds). Mitigations: acceptance sweep on the 15 decides all vs leaf default; C2's translator change (drop the join-key IS NOT NULL Filter) removes the distortion.",
   "q21: RIGHT ANTI is emulated as a right outer join + IS NULL filter and LEFT SEMI has the l2 lineitem scan on its build side; DuckDB must flip both by estimate (it does so measurably for q04's semi join). If it does not, a ~73 GB hash build OOMs (fail-fast bounds it). P5's native LEFT_ANTI/RIGHT_ANTI in the Substrait consumer is the follow-up.",
   "Translation refusals unique to fused shapes (carried columns are handled by confining at the graft; node/tuple/slot ids are query-global) would fail the query loudly via fetch_data rather than the sender RPC; off restores today's path per CN without rebuild.",

- ooc-sort-dev: Use when developing, building, testing, or iterating on the disk-backed (out-of-core) sort implementation for cudf-polars in ~/bzaitlen/test-data/ooc-sort/. Covers installing into the rapidsmpf container env, running streaming sort tests, and the phase-by-phase implementation workflow.

Use when standing the stack up from scratch, recovering a broken toolchain (g++/ld/nvml shims, CUDA 13, no-root conda deps), applying the StarRocks proto patch, or relocating pixi/cargo/Maven onto local NVMe.

Use when choosing GPU_MEM, STAGING, HOST_MEM, hash_partition_bytes, scan_task_batch_size, or when a query OOMs / exhausts the exchange arena / looks like an engine bug that is actually mis-sizing. Covers the derived-flag path vs a full sirius.yaml.

- log-analyzer: Use this skill to analyze Sirius query execution logs — to find why a query is slow, diagnose validation errors (wrong results), spot excessive downgrading, identify pipeline gaps, or compare two runs of the same query. Trigger whenever the user mentions a Sirius log file, says "look at this log", asks about per-operator time, pipeline gaps, memory pressure, downgrade behavior, validation/correctness mismatches, or wants to compare two query runs. Also use as a hand-off target from race-check (for two-run comparisons), runtime-errors (for "where did the query stall before hang"), and validate (for diffing the bad run against a good run). This is the log-only counterpart to profile-analyzer (nsys) and optimization-advisor (source-level guidance).

Use PROACTIVELY before implementing features, fixing bugs, or writing new operators — analyzes the task description and loads cudf, rmm, duckdb, cucascade module docs to improve code quality. Trigger when the user asks to implement, add, fix, or modify GPU operators, pipeline components, memory management, joins, aggregations, sorting, expressions, or data I/O.
- module-discover: Discover and document a dependency library or submodule — analyzes all uses within the codebase, divides the library into logical modules, identifies which modules are used, and generates LLM-consumable API documentation for each module. Use when the user wants to understand a library dependency, map its modules, or generate API reference docs for a submodule.
- optimization-advisor: Use this skill to find exactly which source code to optimize for better GPU performance. Maps nsys profile hotspots to specific Sirius source files and functions, classifies bottlenecks as GPU-bound, CPU-bound, or sync-bound, and recommends actionable code changes. Trigger when the user wants to know what to optimize, where to focus coding effort, or wants source-level optimization guidance. This skill focuses on actionable source code targets — for generating performance reports and measurements, use profile-analyzer instead.
- pr-digest: Generates a "learning" PR-review digest — a markdown file at PR_digests/PR_digest_<N>.md that explains what a GitHub PR does, why, and exactly where in the code, with clickable file/line links and trimmed diffs. Use this whenever the user shares a GitHub PR URL (e.g. github.com/owner/repo/pull/1234) and wants to understand, summarize, review, walk through, or get up to speed on what changed — phrases like "can you review this PR", "what does this PR do", "help me understand this pull request", "summarize the changes in PR
- pre-commit-cleanup: Clean the current Git changes before committing. Use when preparing to commit or when the pre-commit cleanliness hook blocks a commit.

Trigger when the user mentions profiling, nsys, GPU utilization, kernel analysis, performance reports, or wants to compare query timings across runs. 1	# Plan: best solutions for the four SF1000 blockers, and the workflows that deliver them
2	
3	Written 2026-09-03 15:20 UTC from the report `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md`
4	(sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/` (indexed by `WORKFLOW-PLAN.md` there).
5	Working tree for all code: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-*` worktrees of the sirius-stacks clone,
6	one branch per fix off `perf/profile-sf1000` (45dab3be = d24f02c4 + aggregate gate + async dispatch + Quent probes).
7	Never the shared clone `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius`. No pushes, no PRs until asked.
8	
9	## The four issues
10	
11	| # | issue | where it lives | measured cost today (SF1000, 1 CN, 100 GiB pool) |
12	|---|---|---|---|
13	| 1 | The OOM reschedule loop has no feasibility check | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp` (:263 reservation gate, :330-420 reschedule, MAX_RETRIES=100, 50 ms sleep) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 take 54-232 s to die (775 s of a 910 s sweep); 17,917 "0 bytes freed, proceeding with partial reservation" lines |
14	| 2 | No per-query parked-output bookkeeping | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs` (:291-316 process-wide wipe on Err), `compute_node_service.rs` (:449-476 cancel is result-store only), `local_exchange.rs` (removals only in take_ready) | 0-38 GB of a dead query's parked output survives into later queries; dead query's queued senders still run (q22 cold 4110 vs 943 ms) |
15	| 3 | The FE plans every FILES() scan at 1 row | StarRocks FE `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (:664-676), `TableFunctionTable.java` (file sizes at :611, schema RPC), `PGetFileSchemaResult` (proto :647-650), CN `file_schema.rs` | every distribution decision is data-blind: 1 CN broadcasts 3.79B lineitem rows into q04's semi join, 4 CNs shuffle 3.23B rows for q03; all six failures are one plan shape |
16	| 4 | Six queries cannot run on 1 CN | fragment cut (FE) + receiver-first full materialisation (`engine.rs` run_fragment_inner, `local_exchange.rs`) + parked repositories outside the downgrade sweep (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300`) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 OOM; standalone Sirius runs them in 2.7-6.5 s |
17	
18	## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)
19	
20	1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
21	2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
22	3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
23	4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.
24	
25	## Evaluation criteria (judges score 1-5 each)
26	
27	1. Does it fix the measured failure at SF1000 on this box (which queries, predicted numbers, how verified)?
28	2. Correctness risk and blast radius (which paths change for the 15 passing queries; determinism; cancellation).
29	3. Size and reviewability as an upstream PR (target layer in the carve plan: engine `src/` -> dev PR; CN `experimental/starrocks` -> fork PR; FE -> checked-in patch), tests it needs.
30	4. Effort and dependencies (what must land first; FE rebuild; proto change).
31	5. Measurability: an acceptance test that a reviewer can rerun in minutes plus the SF1000 arm.
32	
33	## Acceptance tests (must exist before implementation is "done")
34	
35	| fix | unit / component test | SF1000 verification (orchestrator-run, one arm at a time) |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| 1 | Catch2 test in `test/cpp/pipeline/` driving a task through the reschedule path with a memory space that never frees: query fails within a bounded number of attempts with the new error text; contention case still retries | 1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21: time-to-fail <= 5 s each (was 54-232 s), error names parked bytes; the 15 passing queries unchanged (warm medians within noise, `compare.py` set unchanged) |
38	| 2 | Rust tests in `engine.rs`/`local_exchange.rs`/`compute_node_service.rs`: failure drops only that query's slots; queued senders of a failed query are skipped; cancel drops parked outputs; translation failure drops slots in hand | 1 CN sweep in the same order as before: `[gpu_pool] allocated` returns to baseline after each failure (was +4.7..+38 GB), q22 cold no longer inflated, no `fragment run started` for a dead query after its failure |
39	| 3 | FE unit test (Java) for the new statistics path; CN test if the proto changes; `EXPLAIN COSTS` golden outputs for q03 q04 q05 q22 at 1 and 4 CNs showing real cardinalities and the new join sides | 1 CN and 4 CN sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six: plan shapes recorded, timings vs the campaign table, oracle compares |
40	| 4 | Fusion: translator/CN tests that a single-destination local exchange fuses and the fused plan matches the sender+receiver plan; spill: Catch2 test that a parked repository is swept to HOST and relayed back | 1 CN: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass with oracle MATCH; report their times against standalone (2.7-6.5 s) |
41	
42	## Workflows
43	
44	**A. Design exploration (`fix/design-workflow.js`).** Per issue, three independent designers with different angles (surgical minimum, robust design, what upstream would accept), each reads the report finding, the evidence and the code and returns a design (mechanism, files, tests, risks, predicted effect). Two judges per issue score the three against the criteria and pick or merge. One synthesizer per issue writes the spec `scratchpad/fix/designs/<issue>-SPEC.md`. A final integrator checks the four specs for interactions (fail-fast vs bookkeeping ordering; fusion vs spill vs cardinalities) and writes the build order.
45	
46	**B. Implementation (`fix/implement-workflow.js`).** Per issue in its own worktree: implementer (tests first, then code, build, run the unit tests; commits with Conventional Commits and the Claude trailer), adversarial reviewer, fixer, verifier (fresh build + tests + clippy/fmt/pre-commit). Agents never start clusters or use GPUs other than the one assigned to their worktree (fix 1: GPU 0, fix 2: GPU 1, fix 3: none, fix 4: GPU 2). The orchestrator then runs the SF1000 arms from the table above, one at a time, and an integration branch with all four for the final sweep.

48	**C. Report.** `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-top4-fixes-report.md`: per fix, what changed, tests, SF1000 before/after, what is left; plus the PR plan (branch, base, size) for when pushing is asked for.

Fuse an exchange edge `S -> (R, E)` on the CN *before translation* whenever the sender fragment `S`
has exactly one destination, that destination is this CN, the receiver `R` is registered and still
pending, and `R.per_exch_num_senders[E] == 1`. Fusion is pure bookkeeping in `LocalExchange` (the
receiver keeps `S`'s thrift params under the exchange node id it replaces, and inherits `S`'s own
exchange inputs through an instance-id redirect) plus one translator extension (`translate_exchange`
translates the grafted sender plan in place of the stream read). No C++ engine change is needed:
the fused plan is an ordinary, larger Substrait plan that the engine's own DuckDB optimizer
re-plans with parquet cardinalities, which is exactly the standalone shape that passed all six
queries (`standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv`). On 1 CN every exchange is local and single-sender, so a
query collapses to one fragment per two-phase aggregation boundary (those boundaries are kept, see
section 3.4). The change is Rust-only (translator crate + CN), guarded by one enum knob
`SIRIUS_CN_FRAGMENT_FUSION = off | leaf | all` (default `all`), logs every fuse/skip decision with a
reason, and enumerates its failure modes in section 8.

1	# Fix 4, surgical angle: fuse single-destination local leaf senders into their receiver at the TPlan level
2	
3	Design for "make the six failing queries run on 1 CN", written 2026-09-03 against worktree
4	`/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` at `45dab3be` (all `file:line` below are that tree; evidence
5	paths are relative to the session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/`). Every number is **measured** (with its file) or
6	marked **inference**.
7	
8	## 0. Summary
9	
10	One CN-side change, no engine, translator, FE, proto or wire change:
11	
12	> When a **leaf** sender fragment (no `EXCHANGE_NODE` of its own) arrives with a `DATA_STREAM_SINK` whose
13	> partitioning is `HASH_PARTITIONED` and whose **only** destination is a receiver **on this CN** that is already
14	> registered and expects **exactly one** sender on that exchange, do not run the sender. Store its
15	> `TExecPlanFragmentParams` in the rendezvous as a new `SenderSource::LocalFused`. When the receiver's sender set
16	> completes, splice the sender's `TPlan.nodes` into the receiver's `TPlan` in place of the `EXCHANGE_NODE`, merge
17	> its scan ranges, drop the exchange from `per_exch_num_senders`, and translate/run the fused plan as one fragment.
18	
19	The six failing fragments are exactly this shape (P1): a bare lineitem `FileScanNode` under a one-destination
20	`HASH_PARTITIONED` sink. A shuffle to one destination is a degenerate partitioning; the FE meant a partitioned
21	join, and on one node a partitioned join is a local join. After fusion the lineitem scan sits inside the join
22	fragment, the engine's own optimizer puts it on the probe side (it already does this today for streams, P5/q04),
23	and lineitem streams through the join instead of being parked whole. Broadcast (`UNPARTITIONED`) senders, merge
24	aggregations, sorted/limited exchanges and non-leaf senders are deliberately left exactly as they are today.
25	
26	Predicted outcome at SF1000 / 1 CN / 100 GiB pool: **q05, q08, q17, q18 pass** (high confidence), **q09 passes
27	with little headroom** (medium), **q21 most likely still OOMs** (medium confidence; the reason and the number are
28	in section 6). Of the 15 passing queries, 11 are plan-for-plan identical; q02, q07, q13 and q20 lose 8 parked
29	leaves between them (q07: 59.5 GB less parked) and are expected to get faster. 4-CN behaviour is untouched
30	(a shuffle there has 4 destinations).
31	
32	## 1. What is measured about the failure (facts relied on)
33	
34	1. Six 1-CN failures, one shape. `survey/plan-summary.txt` lines 10, 16, 18, 34, 36, 42 and the dumps
35	   `cn1/dump/fragment-0141` (q05 node 8 -> dest 9), `0208` (q08 node 3 -> 4), `0220` (q09 node 3 -> 4), `0427`
36	   (q17 node 0 -> 1), `0437` (q18 node 9 -> 10), `0504` (q21 node 12 -> 13). My parse of those dumps
37	   (`fix/designs/all-dumps.txt`, produced by `fix/designs/parse_dumps.py`) shows for all six:
38	   `sink=T0` (DATA_STREAM_SINK), `optype=2` (= `HASH_PARTITIONED`, `Partitions.thrift:41-49`), `ndest=1`,
39	   `sender_id=0`, `output_exprs=None`, `output_columns=None`, a single `FILE_SCAN_NODE` (`T17/c0`) with
40	   conjuncts and `limit -1`, and `per_exch_num_senders={}` (a leaf).
41	2. The receiving exchange in each case expects one sender and is a plain exchange: `per_exch` entries are all
42	   `:1`, the exchange nodes are `T9/c0 ... lim-1/noconj ... nosort off=0 ptype=2` (q05 fragment-0137 node 9;
43	   q08 0206 node 4; q09 0214 node 4; q17 0426 node 1 and 4; q18 0433 node 10, 1, 4; q21 0500 node 13, 2, 9).
44	   The exchange's `row_tuples` equals its `input_row_tuples` equals the sender root's `row_tuples` in every
45	   case (e.g. q05: exchange `9:T9 rt[6] irt=[6]`, sender root `8:T17 rt[6]`).
46	3. The sender must park its whole projection because nothing streams across a fragment boundary (B1):
47	   `engine.rs:278-280` one request at a time; `run_fragment_inner` (`engine.rs:486-720`) does declare ->
48	   `build()` -> `relay_from` -> `run()` -> park; `sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745` `relay_from` requires the source to
49	   have run; `local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready` releases a receiver only when every sender is complete.
50	   Parked bytes at death 104.30 / 99.54 / 96.42 / 66.26 / 35.87 / 25.37 GB against a 107.4 GB cap (P1 table;
51	   `cn1-quent.txt` q05 `STREAMING_SINK(1) n=40 in=104.30GB` at line ~352, q17 `66.26GB` at ~1072, q18 `35.87GB`
52	   at ~1093, q21 `25.37GB` at ~1258).
53	4. Parked batches are invisible to the downgrade sweep (B2): `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`
54	   ("Repositories escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup"); `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`
55	   TIER 1 iterates registered managers only, `:294-300` TIER 2 the task queue; 17,917 "0 bytes freed" lines.
56	   `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066 output_row_count` and `:822-825 export_packed` throw on non-GPU batches.
57	5. Standalone Sirius on the same GPU and pool runs all six (`results-failed.md`, `compare-standalone-failed.txt`
58	   all MATCH): warm 2786 / 3674 / 5427 / 3786 / 2691 / 6401 ms. It streams lineitem as the probe of hash joins
59	   built on the small side (`standalone-failed/runs/q05.explain.txt:50-61`; `standalone-failed-quent.txt`:
60	   q05 `GPU_SCAN(27) n=65 in=171.00GB`, q17 `HASH_JOIN(18) n=46 in=120.54GB`).
61	6. The engine already flips join sides inside a fragment from cardinalities it can see: q04 F00
62	   `HASH_JOIN (id=6) type: RIGHT_SEMI` with build = orders scan and probe = the 3.79B-row lineitem stream
63	   (`cn1/engine-cn0.log:48480`, query begun 13:03:38.958 at `:48424`), i.e. DuckDB's build/probe optimizer runs
64	   on the CN path (`duckdb/src/optimizer/build_probe_side_optimizer.cpp:160-212` `TryFlipJoinChildren`, swap
65	   when `right_side_build_cost > left_side_build_cost` at `:185-188`; SEMI/ANTI flipped to RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI
66	   at `:226-240`; `FlipChildren`/`InverseJoinType` at `:55-60`), and the Sirius planner accepts RIGHT_SEMI/
67	   RIGHT_ANTI (`src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:242-246`). The FFI path disables only IN_CLAUSE,
68	   COMPRESSED_MATERIALIZATION, STATISTICS_PROPAGATION, COLUMN_LIFETIME, LATE_MATERIALIZATION
69	   (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:233-240`); join ordering and build/probe selection stay on.
70	7. Receivers are dispatched before their senders. The FE deploys fragment groups root-first
71	   (`ExecutionDAG.java:169-200` javadoc: "All the upstream fragments of the fragments in a group must belong to
72	   the previous groups. Each group should be delivered sequentially"; `Deployer.java:208-215` `deployAsync` then
73	   `waitForDeploymentCompletion` per stage). Measured for q05: the first four `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs closed at
74	   13:03:43.358-43.373 with sub-ms busy time (receivers registering), the nation/region leaves ran at 43.375 and
75	   43.384, the lineitem leaf started at 43.434 (`cn1/cluster.log:4142-4202`). The CN's own module doc says the
76	   same: `local_exchange.rs:3` "StarRocks' receiver-first dispatch".

78	## 2. The CN path today, and where the change goes

165	## 3. Mechanism
166	
167	### 3.1 Fusability predicate (pure, on thrift only)
168	
169	`fusable_leaf_sender(sender: &TExecPlanFragmentParams) -> Result<Option<(ExchangeKey, i32 /*sender_id*/)>, String>`
170	returns `Some` iff all of:
171	
172	- `SIRIUS_CN_FUSE_LOCAL_LEAVES` is not `0|false|off` (read once at bring-up, same pattern as
173	  `async_sender_dispatch_from_env`, `compute_node_service.rs:289-296`; `#[cfg(test)]` setter);
174	- `receiver_exchanges(sender)?.is_empty()` (a leaf: no `EXCHANGE_NODE` in its plan);
175	- the sink is `DATA_STREAM_SINK` with `stream_sink.limit` unset/negative and `output_columns` None/empty;
176	- `stream_sink.output_partition.type_ == TPartitionType::HASH_PARTITIONED`;
177	- `destinations.len() == 1` and `route_destination(&destinations[0])? == Local`;
178	- `fragment.output_exprs` is None/empty (the six leaves have none; a sender with output exprs would need a
179	  PROJECT splice, decline instead).
180	
181	`fusable_receiver_exchange(receiver: &TExecPlanFragmentParams, node_id, sender_root: &TPlanNode) -> Result<(), &'static str>`
182	(evaluated under the rendezvous lock, on the registered receiver's params):
183	
184	- an `EXCHANGE_NODE` with `node_id` exists, `num_children == 0`, `limit == -1`, no `conjuncts`,
185	  `exchange_node.sort_info.is_none()`, `offset.unwrap_or(0) == 0` (merging/limited exchanges stay streams);
186	- `exchange.row_tuples == sender_root.row_tuples` (the ExchangeNode.java:183-186 guarantee, checked rather
187	  than assumed);
188	- the exchange's parent in preorder is **not** an `AGGREGATION_NODE` (conservative superset of "merge
189	  aggregation": keeps `merge_exchange_overrides` (node_translator.rs:438-470) satisfied and leaves two-phase
190	  aggregation, which is cheap (AGG-5, 3-24 ms), exactly as today). Parent lookup is the standard preorder
191	  ancestor stack already used by `common_slots_consumed_above` (node_translator.rs:504-560); ~15 lines.
192	
193	Anything else is a *decline* (fall back to today's run-and-park), never an error: fusion is an optimisation
194	with a complete fallback, so a wrong guess costs performance, not correctness.
195	
196	### 3.2 Rendezvous: a third source kind

203	    /// Holds thrift only (tens of KB); no GPU memory.

205	}

207	
208	pub(crate) enum FuseOffer { Fused(Option<ReadyFragment>), Declined(&'static str) }
209	
210	/// Offers a leaf sender for fusion. Under the lock: the receiver must be registered, expect exactly one
211	/// sender on `key.node_id`, have no source for it yet, and its exchange node must pass
212	/// `fusable_receiver_exchange`. On success records `LocalFused` and runs `take_ready`.
213	pub(crate) fn offer_fused_sender(&self, key: ExchangeKey, sender_id: i32, params: TExecPlanFragmentParams) -> Result<FuseOffer, String>
214	```

255	### 3.5 The splice (pure function, new file `experimental/starrocks/src/fragment_fusion.rs`)
256	
257	```rust
258	pub(crate) fn splice_leaf(mut receiver: TExecPlanFragmentParams, node_id: i32, sender: &TExecPlanFragmentParams)
259	    -> Result<TExecPlanFragmentParams, String>
260	{
261	    let plan = receiver.fragment.as_mut()?.plan.as_mut()?;
262	    let pos = plan.nodes.iter().position(|n| n.node_id == node_id && n.node_type == TPlanNodeType::EXCHANGE_NODE)?;
263	    let leaf = &sender.fragment.as_ref()?.plan.as_ref()?.nodes;
264	    // The exchange is a preorder leaf (num_children == 0) and `leaf` is a complete preorder subtree rooted at
265	    // leaf[0]; replacing one leaf entry by a subtree keeps every ancestor's `num_children` valid.
266	    plan.nodes.splice(pos..=pos, leaf.iter().cloned());
267	
268	    let exec = receiver.params.as_mut()?; let sexec = sender.params.as_ref()?;
269	    exec.per_exch_num_senders.remove(&node_id);
270	    for (nid, ranges) in &sexec.per_node_scan_ranges {
271	        if exec.per_node_scan_ranges.insert(*nid, ranges.clone()).is_some() { return Err(format!("scan node {nid} already present in receiver")); }
272	    }
273	    if let Some(per_driver) = &sexec.node_to_per_driver_seq_scan_ranges { /* same merge into exec.node_to_per_driver_seq_scan_ranges */ }
274	    Ok(receiver)
275	}
276	```
277	
278	Both maps are merged because `ScanFilePaths::from_fragment` reads both (`scan_paths.rs:70-90`) and enforces that a
279	node appears in exactly one; node ids are query-global so keys cannot collide with the receiver's own scans
280	(q21 F00 has its own `FileScanNode 0`).

459	## 10. Risks
460	
461	1. **Estimated instead of exact cardinality for fused leaves** (the q21 mechanism above). Bounded to shuffle
462	   leaves under non-aggregation parents; the only way it hurts is a wrong build side, which is a memory/time
463	   regression not a wrong answer. Mitigation: the gate, the A/B arm, and the per-query fused-count check.
464	2. **Order dependence**: fusion needs the receiver registered before the leaf arrives. Guaranteed by the FE's
465	   default stage-by-stage deploy (section 1 item 7) and measured for q05. Under `enable_single_node_schedule`
466	   (`DefaultCoordinator.java:697-704`, `Deployer.java:359-390` deploys everything at once) RPCs can race; the
467	   design then *declines* and behaves exactly as today (logged). An order-independent variant (hold the leaf's
468	   params under the exchange key, decide at `register_receiver`) is ~30 more lines and can follow if that
469	   scheduler is ever enabled.
470	3. **Translator invariants on the spliced plan**: `merge_exchange_overrides` (protected by the aggregation-parent
471	   decline), `common_slots_consumed_above`'s preorder ancestor stack (preserved by a leaf-for-subtree splice),
472	   `refuse_carried_join_child` (a spliced scan/project carries nothing a stream would not; both come from the
473	   same FE descriptor row). Test 11 exercises the translator on a spliced plan.
474	4. **Dumps/tooling**: `fragment-NNNN.txt` for a fused receiver is the fused plan (deliberate, pairs with the
475	   substrait); `cnlog_extract.py`'s `frags=` counts shrink. Note it in the report.
476	5. **Failure attribution**: a fused receiver's failure is attributed to the receiver's instance id (as any
477	   receiver failure); the absorbed leaf's id never appears in `fragment run started/finished`. Cancel is
478	   unaffected (`cancel_plan_fragment` is result-store only today, `compute_node_service.rs:449-476`).
479	6. **4 CNs**: unaffected by construction (`destinations.len() > 1`, or a remote route, declines).
480	7. **Nothing spills**: this design does not make the six robust to larger SFs or smaller pools; it removes one
481	   plan shape's need to park. q09 at 70-90 GB predicted peak is the canary.

2	
3	Written 2026-09-03 for the SF1000 top-4 plan (`sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md`, issue 4). Source tree
4	read: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` at `45dab3be`. Evidence:
5	`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/` (cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1/dump, standalone-failed/, results-ratios.md) and the

11	
12	## 0. Decision in one paragraph
13	
14	Fuse an exchange edge `S -> (R, E)` on the CN *before translation* whenever the sender fragment `S`
15	has exactly one destination, that destination is this CN, the receiver `R` is registered and still
16	pending, and `R.per_exch_num_senders[E] == 1`. Fusion is pure bookkeeping in `LocalExchange` (the
17	receiver keeps `S`'s thrift params under the exchange node id it replaces, and inherits `S`'s own
18	exchange inputs through an instance-id redirect) plus one translator extension (`translate_exchange`
19	translates the grafted sender plan in place of the stream read). No C++ engine change is needed:
20	the fused plan is an ordinary, larger Substrait plan that the engine's own DuckDB optimizer
21	re-plans with parquet cardinalities, which is exactly the standalone shape that passed all six
22	queries (`standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv`). On 1 CN every exchange is local and single-sender, so a
23	query collapses to one fragment per two-phase aggregation boundary (those boundaries are kept, see
24	section 3.4). The change is Rust-only (translator crate + CN), guarded by one enum knob
25	`SIRIUS_CN_FRAGMENT_FUSION = off | leaf | all` (default `all`), logs every fuse/skip decision with a
26	reason, and enumerates its failure modes in section 8.
27	
28	The engine-side alternative (spillable parked repositories, plan item 4(b)) is not chosen: it keeps
29	the full materialisation that finding B1 identifies as the root cause, needs C++ changes in four
30	places (`streaming_fragment.cpp:103-113`, `downgrade_executor.cpp:203-232`, `sirius_ffi.cpp:822-826`
31	and `:1062-1066`), and even at 279 GB GPU+HOST rescues five of six slowly with q09 marginal
32	(B2 impact arithmetic). It stays the right tool for *multi*-CN shuffle/broadcast receivers, which
33	fusion by construction does not touch. Section 10 has the side-by-side.
34

242	## 3. Mechanism
243	
244	### 3.1 Vocabulary
245	
246	- **Fusable edge**: sender fragment `S` -> receiver fragment `R` at exchange node `E`, where
247	  `S.destinations.len() == 1`, `route_destination(dest) == Local`, `R` is a pending receiver on
248	  this CN whose `expected_senders[E] == 1`, and the structural checks of 3.3 pass.
249	- **Graft**: `R` records `S.params` under `E`; `E` leaves `R.expected_senders`; `S`'s own
250	  exchange inputs (if any) join `R.expected_senders`; `S.instance -> R.instance` is recorded in an
251	  `absorbed` redirect map so anything later addressed to `S` (senders, remote frames, cancels)
252	  reaches `R`.
253	- **Fused translation**: when `R` becomes ready, the translator lowers `R`'s plan with
254	  `translate_exchange(E)` producing the translated sender subtree instead of a stream read.
255	
256	### 3.2 Where the decision is made: sender arrival
257	
258	New `ServiceCore::try_fuse(&params) -> Result<Option<FragmentOutcome>, String>` runs before
259	`try_dispatch_sender` in both entry points (`exec_single_attachment` `:705-717` and the per-instance
260	loop in `translate_batch_attachment` `:1646-1676`). Steps:
261	
262	1. `resolve_descriptor_table` and `dump_fragment` exactly as today (the survey tooling keeps seeing
263	   every FE fragment; `SIRIUS_CN_TRANSLATE_ONLY` skips fusion entirely).
264	2. Read the knob. `off` -> return `None`. `leaf` -> only a sender with no `EXCHANGE_NODE` is a
265	   candidate. `all` -> any sender.
266	3. Sink shape: `output_sink.type_ == DATA_STREAM_SINK`, `destinations.len() == 1`, destination
267	   routes `Local`, `stream_sink.limit` unset, `stream_sink.output_columns` identity or absent,
268	   `fragment.output_exprs` empty. Anything else -> `None` with a logged reason (these are the same
269	   conditions `execute_fragment_with_inputs` already enforces or that would change the sink row,
270	   `:1079-1094`). **Measured:** none of the six leaf senders carries `output_exprs`
271	   (`grep -c "output_exprs: Some" fragment-{0141,0208,0220,0427,0437,0504}.txt` = 0; the 151
272	   fragments that do are result fragments, e.g. `fragment-0134.txt`).
273	4. Ask the translator for the structural verdict: `PlanTranslator::exchange_fusability(receiver,
274	   sender, E)` (3.3). This needs the receiver's params, so it is evaluated inside the
275	   `LocalExchange` lock via a closure (3.5).
276	5. `self.exchanges.try_fuse_sender(key, params, sender_exchanges, verdict_fn)`:
277	   - `Fused(None)`: `S` is absorbed, `R` still waits -> the RPC returns OK immediately, nothing
278	     runs. Log `fused sender fragment into its local receiver` with `query_id`, `sender_instance`,
279	     `receiver_instance`, `exchange_node_id`, `inherited_exchanges`.
280	   - `Fused(Some(ready))`: the graft completed `R` -> `dispatch_then_join(FragmentOutcome::from_ready(vec![ready]))`,
281	     the same path a completing sender takes today (`:716`).
282	   - `NotFused(reason)`: fall through to today's behaviour (async queue or run+park). Log
283	     `fragment fusion skipped` with the reason enum (`NoPendingReceiver`, `ReceiverExpectsMany(n)`,
284	     `ExchangeAlreadySourced`, `PolicyLeafOnly`, `Structural(<translator reason>)`).
285	
286	`process_fragment` is otherwise unchanged; a sender that was not fused still registers as a
287	receiver (if it has exchanges) or runs.
288	
289	### 3.3 Structural fusability (translator, pure function over thrift)
290	
291	`exchange_fusability(receiver: &TExecPlanFragmentParams, sender: &TExecPlanFragmentParams, node_id: i32) -> Result<(), FusionRefusal>`:
292	
293	| check | why | refusal |
294	|---|---|---|

417	### 3.6 Behaviour under the two dispatch orders
418	
419	- **Receiver first (measured FE order, 2.6):** every fusable edge fuses at sender arrival. On 1 CN
420	  a query collapses to `1 + (#merge-fed exchanges)` fragments.
421	- **Sender first (not observed; defensive):** `NotFused(NoPendingReceiver)` -> the sender runs and
422	  parks exactly as today; the receiver, when it arrives, sees a parked source and reads a stream.
423	  Correct, slower, logged at `info` so a change in FE behaviour is visible in the CN log.
424	
425	There is no third state: a sender is either absorbed (never runs on its own) or runs today's path.
426	Nothing is ever held waiting for a fragment that may not come, so fusion cannot introduce a hang.

445	### 3.8 Cancellation and the interaction with fix 2
446	
447	Fusion adds two pieces of per-query host state to `LocalExchange`: `PendingReceiver.fused`
448	(thrift params of absorbed senders, hundreds of KB each) and `absorbed` entries. Neither pins GPU
449	memory. Today `cancel_plan_fragment` (`:457-479`) only touches the result store, and
450	`LocalExchange` removes state only in `take_ready` (`:282-308`) — B4. Fix 2's design adds a
451	by-query removal (`LocalExchange::remove_query(query_id)` or equivalent). This design requires that
452	removal to also drop `fused` (it goes with the `PendingReceiver`) and `absorbed` entries whose
453	owner is that query (store `query_id` on `PendingReceiver`, or derive it from
454	`params.params.query_id` at removal time). If fusion lands before fix 2, it ships a minimal
455	`LocalExchange::forget_query(query_id)` for its own maps and `cancel_plan_fragment` calls it;
456	fix 2 then subsumes it. Without either, the cost of a cancelled query is a bounded host-memory
457	leak of thrift params, not a GPU leak — strictly better than today, where the same query's senders
458	would run and park GPU output nobody consumes (B4).

1	# Design: same-node fragment fusion at the TPlan level (issue 4, "what upstream would accept" angle)
2	
3	Written 2026-09-03 from the SF1000 report (P1, P5, B1, B2, section 4), the evidence bundle
4	`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/`, and the source worktree `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf`
5	at `45dab3be`. Every line number below was read from that worktree. "Measured" means copied from
6	a named evidence file; everything else is marked inference.
7	
8	## 0. One paragraph
9	
10	On 1 CN the FE still cuts every query into fragments and the CN parks a whole exchange input on the
11	GPU before the receiver can start (B1). The six failures are a bare `lineitem` scan under a
12	one-destination `HASH_PARTITIONED` sink whose projection (122-245 GB) cannot be parked in a 100 GiB
13	pool (P1). The design: when a data-stream sender's only destination is a receiver **on this CN**
14	whose exchange node expects **exactly one sender**, do not run the sender. Park its *plan* in the
15	rendezvous instead of its *rows*, and when the receiver becomes ready splice the sender's `TPlan`
16	node list in place of the receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE`, merge the scan ranges, and translate the
17	fused fragment as one plan. The engine then sees the lineitem scan as an ordinary `ReadRel` inside
18	the join fragment, DuckDB's optimizer (which already runs on every fragment, `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:131-135`)
19	puts the 6.0e9-row scan on the probe side, and the scan streams through the hash join exactly as it
20	does in standalone Sirius, which passes all six in 2.7-6.5 s. No engine change, no FE change, no
21	proto change; the FE never learns the sender did not run because the CN reports nothing per
22	instance (no `report_exec_status` anywhere under `experimental/starrocks/src/`). Two-phase
23	aggregation and merging (sorted) exchanges are deliberately left as stream boundaries: they carry
24	the small aggregate outputs and the translator's partial-state model depends on the boundary
25	(`node_translator.rs:438-496`). No `RIGHT_SEMI` translator arm is needed: the flip happens inside
26	the engine after fusion, as it already does today for q04 (`cn1/engine-cn0.log:48480`,
27	`HASH_JOIN (id=6) type: RIGHT_SEMI`).
28	
29	## 1. What the code does today (verified mechanism)
30	
31	### 1.1 Receiver-first rendezvous, one fragment at a time
32	
33	- `compute_node_service.rs:918-959 process_fragment`: a fragment with `EXCHANGE_NODE`s is
34	  registered as a receiver and returns (`:934-949`); a fragment with none is translated and run
35	  (`:958-959`). `receiver_exchanges` (`:1398-1432`) reads `per_exch_num_senders` per exchange node.
36	- `compute_node_service.rs:1021-1245 execute_fragment_with_inputs`: a `DATA_STREAM_SINK` fragment
37	  runs on the engine (`run_labeled("sender", ...)`, `:1173-1186`) with one output stream per
38	  destination, then each **local** destination is pushed into the rendezvous as
39	  `SenderSource::LocalParked { names, slot }` (`:1189-1206`). One destination is a gather regardless
40	  of partition label (`:1104-1111`).
41	- `local_exchange.rs:26-48 SenderSource` has two variants, `LocalParked` (complete by construction,
42	  `:59-64`) and `Remote`. `register_receiver` (`:105-139`) stores `PendingReceiver { params,
43	  expected_senders }`; `take_ready` (`:248-313`) releases the receiver once every exchange has
44	  `expected` complete sources.
45	- `compute_node_service.rs:1312-1395 execute_ready_fragment`: builds one `ExchangeInput` per
46	  exchange (sender names + `sirius_stream_<node_id>` view), translates with
47	  `translate_fragment_logged_with_inputs`, and runs with the parked slots.
48	- `engine.rs:486-733 run_fragment_inner`: declare stream columns and senders (`:510-549`), declare
49	  the **exact** parked row count (`:551-587`, `output_row_count`), `build()` (`:610-612`),
50	  `relay_from` every parked sender (`:616-647`), `run()`, park the output (`:697-716`). The engine
51	  is single-flight (`Fragment::build()` takes the query lifecycle slot, B1), so the sender must have
52	  finished and parked everything before the receiver's `relay_from` (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:735-745`
53	  refuses a source that has not run).
54	- `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-113`: sink output repositories and receiver input
55	  repositories are created outside `data_repository_manager`, so the downgrade sweep
56	  (`src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:203-291` TIER 1 over `_data_repo_registry.get_all()`,
57	  `:293-345` TIER 2 pipeline queue) never sees a parked batch (B2). `Fragment::output_row_count`
58	  (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:1050-1071`) and `export_packed` (`:803-888`) throw on a non-GPU batch.
59	
60	### 1.2 What a fused plan needs to be valid
61	
62	- **Row layout.** The FE's `ExchangeNode` copies its child's tuple ids:
63	  `ExchangeNode.java:181-184 computeTupleIds() { tupleIds.addAll(getChild(0).getTupleIds()); ... }`
64	  and ships them as `input_row_tuples` (`ExchangeNode.java:360`). Confirmed in the q05 dumps: the
65	  lineitem sender root has `row_tuples: [6]` (`cn1/dump/fragment-0141.txt:11-19`, node 8) and the
66	  receiver's exchange 9 has `input_row_tuples: [6]` (`cn1/dump/fragment-0137.txt:3020-3022`).
67	  The translator resolves slot refs through `row_tuples` (`DescriptorTable::slot_global_index`,
68	  `lib.rs` module doc "Adding a node" step 3), so the parent's expressions resolve identically
69	  whether the child is the exchange or the sender's root.
70	- **Flat preorder.** `TPlan.nodes` is a preorder list with `num_children` per node
71	  (`lib.rs:12-22`). An `EXCHANGE_NODE` has `num_children: 0` (`fragment-0137.txt:2541, 3003`), so
72	  replacing that single node by the sender's whole node list (itself a valid preorder) keeps the
73	  parent's `num_children` and `PlanNodeCursor::ensure_consumed` (`node_translator.rs:187-225`)
74	  satisfied.
75	- **Scan ranges** are keyed by scan node id: `scan_paths.rs:62-90` reads
76	  `per_node_scan_ranges` and `node_to_per_driver_seq_scan_ranges`; `translate_scan`
77	  (`node_translator.rs:341-356`) looks up `ctx.scan_paths.for_node(node.node_id)`. Node ids are
78	  query-unique (the FE's `PlanNodeId` generator), so the maps union without collision.
79	- **Descriptor table** is per query: `resolve_descriptor_table` (`compute_node_service.rs:961-996`)
80	  caches the full table sent once and restores it for `is_cached` references, so the receiver's
81	  resolved `desc_tbl` already holds the sender's tuples and slots.
82	- **Exchange-only decorations** that the fused subtree would lose: `TExchangeNode.sort_info` and
83	  `offset` (`PlanNodes.thrift TExchangeNode`, translated at `node_translator.rs:746-775` and
84	  `apply_fetch :258-270`), node `limit` and `conjuncts` (`apply_conjuncts :2461-2494`). In the six
85	  failing plans the join-side exchanges have `limit: -1, conjuncts: None, sort_info: None,
86	  offset: Some(0)` (`fragment-0137.txt:2537-2565` node 7; `:2999-3026` node 9).
87	- **Two-phase aggregation** requires the boundary: `merge_exchange_overrides`
88	  (`node_translator.rs:438-496`) refuses a merge aggregation whose next preorder node is not an
89	  exchange, and a partial aggregation over `avg` must be the fragment root (`:404-414`).
90	- **Common-expr projections**: `common_slots_consumed_above` (`:498-560`) walks ancestors in the
91	  flat list; `refuse_carried_join_child` (`:1880-1895`) refuses carried columns into a join. All
92	  sampled q05 fragments have `common_slot_map: None` (`cn1/dump/fragment-0137/0140/0141/0142/0143/0145/0136`),
93	  so the guard in section 2.2 costs nothing for TPC-H.
94	- **Dispatch order.** The FE deploys fragments root-first, stage by stage:
95	  `ExecutionDAG.java:170-200 getFragmentsInTopologicalOrderFromRoot` ("All the upstream fragments
96	  of the fragments in a group must belong to the previous groups. Each group should be delivered
97	  sequentially") and `Deployer.java:164-215 deployFragments`. Inside one batch RPC the CN processes
98	  instances in FE order (`translate_batch_attachment :1622-1680`). So a receiver is registered
99	  before its sender is processed on both the inline and the `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH`
100	  (`:271-329`) paths.
101	- **The engine already re-plans inside a fragment.** `lower_substrait` runs DuckDB's optimizer
102	  (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:131-135`) with only `IN_CLAUSE, COMPRESSED_MATERIALIZATION,
103	  STATISTICS_PROPAGATION, COLUMN_LIFETIME, LATE_MATERIALIZATION` disabled (`:233-240`);
104	  `JOIN_ORDER` and `BUILD_SIDE_PROBE_SIDE` run. `BuildProbeSideOptimizer::TryFlipJoinChildren`
105	  (`duckdb/src/optimizer/build_probe_side_optimizer.cpp:160-213`) swaps children when
106	  `row_width x estimated_cardinality` of the right (build) side exceeds the left, and turns
107	  `SEMI/ANTI` into `RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI` (`:228-236`). Parquet scans estimate from footers;
108	  non-equality filters take `DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY = 0.2`
109	  (`duckdb/src/include/duckdb/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.hpp:57`,
110	  `relation_statistics_helper.cpp:143-150`, `relation_manager.cpp:199,258,276,293,374`). Measured:
111	  q04's FE plan builds on lineitem, the engine ran `HASH_JOIN (id=6) type: RIGHT_SEMI` with the
112	  orders scan as build (`cn1/engine-cn0.log:48470-48482`, P5). The engine implements
113	  `RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI` (`src/op/sirius_physical_hash_join.cpp:228-231, 2148-2163`;
114	  `src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:241-246, 272-274`).
115	
116	## 2. Mechanism
117	
118	### 2.1 Layering
119	
120	| layer | change | PR target (carve plan) |
121	|---|---|---|
122	| translator crate `experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator` | new `pub mod fusion` with two pure functions over thrift structs; unit tests | fork PR (CI `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `.github/workflows/experimental.yml:76-79`) |
123	| CN `experimental/starrocks/src` | `SenderSource::LocalPlan` variant + a peek in `local_exchange.rs`; a deferral hook before translation and a fold at ready time in `compute_node_service.rs`; one off switch read at bring-up | fork PR, stacked on the translator PR (or one PR of ~600 lines if the reviewer prefers) |
124	| engine `src/` | none | - |
125	| FE patch `experimental/starrocks/patches/` | none | - |
126	| docs | `experimental/starrocks/docs/TUNABLES.md` row; `experimental/starrocks/DEMO.md` "Sequential fragments" paragraph | same PR |
127	
128	### 2.2 Translator: `fusion.rs` (pure, no engine, no I/O)
129	
130	```rust
131	/// Why a receiver exchange keeps its stream boundary instead of absorbing its sender.
132	pub enum FusionRefusal { MergeAggregationParent, SortedExchange, ExchangeLimit, ExchangeConjuncts,
133	    ExchangeOffset, SenderOutputExprs, SenderSinkMismatch, SenderNonIdentityColumns, SenderSinkLimit,
134	    RowTuplesDiffer { exchange: Vec<i32>, sender_root: Vec<i32> }, CommonSlotProjection { node_id: i32 },
135	    ScanRangeCollision { node_id: i32 }, NestedExpansionRoot }
136	
137	/// Checks the receiver side only (the sender is not known yet when the receiver registers).
138	pub fn fusable_exchange(receiver_plan: &TPlan, exchange_node_id: i32) -> Result<(), FusionRefusal>;
139	
140	/// Splices `sender.fragment.plan.nodes` over the receiver's EXCHANGE_NODE, unions the exec params
141	/// the translator reads (`per_node_scan_ranges`, `node_to_per_driver_seq_scan_ranges`,
142	/// `per_exch_num_senders` for exchanges the sender itself still reads), and returns the fused
143	/// params with the RECEIVER's identity (query_id, fragment_instance_id, sink, destinations).
144	pub fn fuse_sender(receiver: &TExecPlanFragmentParams, exchange_node_id: i32,
145	                   sender: &TExecPlanFragmentParams) -> Result<TExecPlanFragmentParams, FusionRefusal>;
146	```
147	
148	`fusable_exchange` walks the flat preorder list with the same span arithmetic as
149	`common_slots_consumed_above` to find the exchange's parent and refuses when:
150	
151	1. the parent is an `AGGREGATION_NODE` classified `AggPhase::Merge` by `agg_phase::classify`
152	   (`agg_phase.rs:45-79`) -- keeps `merge_exchange_overrides` (`node_translator.rs:438-496`) and the
153	   avg root rule (`:404-414`) untouched;
154	2. `exchange_node.sort_info.is_some()` (a MERGING-EXCHANGE, `node_translator.rs:746-761`);
155	3. `node.limit >= 0` or `exchange_node.offset` is `Some(n > 0)` (`apply_fetch :258-270`);
156	4. `node.conjuncts` non-empty (`apply_conjuncts :2461-2494`; fusing would have to re-attach them
157	   above the sender root -- possible, but not needed for TPC-H and not worth the extra path).
158	
159	`fuse_sender` additionally refuses when the sender has `fragment.output_exprs` (non-empty), its
160	sink is not a `DATA_STREAM_SINK` with `dest_node_id == exchange_node_id`, `output_columns` is a
161	non-identity permutation or `limit >= 0` (the same three checks `execute_fragment_with_inputs`
162	already makes at `:1073-1093`), the sender root's `row_tuples != exchange.input_row_tuples`, any
163	`PROJECT_NODE` in the sender carries a non-empty `common_slot_map` (`:498-560, 1880-1895`), or a
164	scan-range key collides. A refusal at this stage is a bug (the receiver-side check passed), so the
165	CN turns it into a loud query failure rather than a silent fallback.
166	
167	Everything the translator does downstream is unchanged: the fused `TPlan` is an ordinary fragment
168	whose remaining `EXCHANGE_NODE`s (the ones that refused) still lower to stream reads
169	(`translate_exchange :637-777`).
170	
171	### 2.3 CN: defer at the sender, fold at the receiver
172	
173	**`local_exchange.rs`**
174	
175	```rust
176	pub(crate) enum SenderSource {
177	    LocalParked { names, slot },
178	    Remote { .. },
179	    /// A same-node sender whose PLAN was deferred into its receiver instead of running. Holds
180	    /// no GPU memory. `inputs` are the exchange inputs the deferred sender itself consumed
181	    /// (parked slots, staged remote batches, or nested deferred plans) so the fused fragment
182	    /// relays them under their own stream ids.
183	    LocalPlan { params: TExecPlanFragmentParams, inputs: Vec<ReadyExchangeInput> },
184	}
185	// is_complete(): LocalPlan => true (nothing to wait for).
186	// names(): only meaningful for LocalParked/Remote; the fold in 2.3 consumes LocalPlan first.
187	
188	/// Peek used by the sender path: is `receiver` pending, how many senders does `node_id` expect,
189	/// and does the receiver's plan accept a fusion at that node? Computed under the lock; nothing
190	/// is cloned but the verdict.
191	pub(crate) fn fusion_verdict(&self, receiver: FragmentInstanceId, node_id: i32) -> Option<FusionVerdict>;
192	```
193	
194	`take_ready` (`:248-313`) is unchanged: a `LocalPlan` counts as a complete sender, so a receiver
195	whose only sender was deferred becomes ready the moment the sender is pushed, and the ready set
196	flows to the dispatch worker exactly as today (`FragmentOutcome`, `dispatch_then_join :351-376`,
197	`dispatch_worker :380-390`).
198	
199	**`compute_node_service.rs`**
200	
201	1. `ServiceCore::try_defer_into_receiver(&self, params, inputs: Vec<ReadyExchangeInput>)
202	   -> Result<Option<Vec<ReadyFragment>>, String>` runs **before translation** in both places a
203	   sender is about to be translated:
204	   - `process_fragment` (`:958`) for a sender with no exchange inputs (leaf), and
205	   - `execute_ready_fragment` (`:1339-1341`) for a receiver that is itself a sender (middle
206	     fragment), passing its own `ready.inputs` along.
207	   It returns `Some(ready)` when all of: the switch is on; the sink is a `DATA_STREAM_SINK` with
208	   exactly one destination and `route_destination` (`:1254-1268`) says `Local`; the sink passes the
209	   existing limit/output_columns checks; `exchanges.fusion_verdict(dest_instance, dest_node_id)`
210	   is `Fusable { expected: 1 }`. Then `exchanges.push_sender(key, sender_id,
211	   SenderSource::LocalPlan { params, inputs })` and the caller treats the result like today's

357	## 5. Risks
358	
359	1. **q21's anti join could flip the wrong way (medium).** The translator lowers `RIGHT ANTI` as
360	   `RIGHT` outer + `IS NULL` (`node_translator.rs:1750, 1837-1844`). After fusion DuckDB compares
361	   `est(l3 filtered) = 6.0e9 x 0.2 = 1.2e9` against its estimate of `l1 x orders-F`. If the join
362	   estimate exceeds 1.2e9 the optimizer builds on l3 (3.8e9 actual rows x 12 B = 46 GB plus a
363	   3.8e9-key table, ~100 GB) and q21 OOMs again; if not (the expected outcome: DuckDB's
364	   join-cardinality estimate without statistics is bounded by the smaller input, ~3e8), the build
365	   is ~40-52 GB and q21 passes. Verify from the fused plan's engine print before the SF1000 arm;
366	   the fallback is the native `LEFT_ANTI/RIGHT_ANTI` lowering (section 4 item 5 of the report),
367	   which does not remove the estimate problem but makes the join an `ANTI` DuckDB can also flip
368	   back. Fix 1 (fail fast) makes the wrong outcome cost ~3 s instead of 114 s.
369	2. **Join order in a fused plan comes from DuckDB without statistics propagation (medium).**
370	   Today a receiver plans with exact stream counts (C2); after fusion a filtered scan is guessed at
371	   0.2. A wrong pick on a big unfiltered relation (q09's orders 1.5e9 / partsupp 8e8) costs memory
372	   but stays under the pool by the arithmetic above; q09 remains the closest to the limit.
373	   Mitigation in-PR: none (this is the standalone planner's information set minus statistics);
374	   follow-up: enable `STATISTICS_PROPAGATION` on the FFI path once GPU_VALUES coverage exists
375	   (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:235-237`).
376	3. **Two-phase aggregation stays a boundary (low, by design).** q18 keeps 24 GB parked and builds
377	   a ~36 GB merge table; passes on arithmetic but is the tightest. Follow-up options: collapse
378	   `update serialize -> exchange -> merge finalize` into one `OneShot` aggregation at fusion time
379	   (needs the intermediate/output tuple remap and the `avg` state model), or the FE session
380	   variable `new_planner_agg_stage = 1` the translator already names in its errors
381	   (`node_translator.rs:462, 1131`).
382	4. **Blast radius on passing queries (low-medium).** Every 1-CN plan with a join-side exchange
383	   changes shape. The acceptance arm compares the 15 warm medians and oracle set; the switch gives
384	   an immediate revert path in the field. 4-CN plans are unchanged.
385	5. **Telemetry and log consumers (low).** A fused sender has no `fragment run started` line and
386	   no Quent query of its own (labels come from the receiver, `engine.rs:499-507`);
387	   `cnlog_extract.py`/`quent_bp.py` counts per query drop. The new `fused` log line carries the
388	   sender instance ids so the stitch stays possible.
389	6. **Deferred sender never runs if the receiver is lost (low).** If the FE cancels the query
390	   before the receiver is ready, the `LocalPlan` sits in `ExchangeState.sources` like a parked
391	   slot does today; it holds no GPU memory. Fix 2's by-query removal in `LocalExchange` should
392	   drop `LocalPlan` sources too (one match arm).

317	**Proposed.** Move `export_packed` off the engine thread (needs `ParkedOutput`/`Fragment` reachable from another thread; the parked map lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272) and make it faster: try a larger `kPackChunkBytes` or a single `cudf::pack` for GPU-resident batches (the receiver-side copy of the same bytes is 30x faster, so the 8 MiB chunking is the suspect; inference, medium confidence). Then (b)/(c) add value. Expected gain 0.15-0.3 s per shuffle stage at 4 CNs for q03/q10/q12 (inference). Confidence high on the mechanism.
318	
319	#### B6 (confirmed). The staging arena is 87-88% full for q03 and q07 at 4 CNs, and exhaustion fails the query instead of applying backpressure
320	
321	**Measured.** cn4 q03.r1 receiver on 9102: stream 2 frames 4.8885 + 4.8423 + 4.8506 GB + 3 x 0.146 (stream 9) + 3 x 0.03 (stream 6) = 15.1 GB = 14.1 GiB of the 16 GiB arena (cn4/cluster.log `received remote batches`); Quent whole-query occupancy peak 14.95-15.10 GB of 17.18 GB per CN at +1.28 s. Frames land at +0.71..+1.01 s and are consumed at +1.30 s (dwell 0.4-0.6 s while the customer and orders x customer fragments run and the receiver waits for all four senders). q07.r1: lineitem 3 x 3.62-3.68 + orders 3 x 1.13 + customer 3 x 0.30 = ~15.2 GB per CN. q10 6.4-11.7 GiB, q12 5.4-6.0, q14 <= 3.3, q19 0.7. Lease waits are zero (cn4-transmits.txt `lease_ms` median 0, max 15 ms in q12.r1), which is consistent with a non-blocking arena, not with "no pressure". Peak lease concurrency per CN: q07.r1 63-64, q03.r1 55-56 (cn4-quent.txt per-fragment `maxconc`; session-wide max 94, WORKFLOW-PLAN fact 13) against no lease-count limit, so the arena is bounded by bytes only; per-query lease counts and GB in cn4-quent.txt are time-attributed and can bleed into the next run (tooling defect AGG-6 below), which is why per-stream bytes above come from cn4/cluster.log rather than from the lease digest.
322	
323	**Source (verified).** `src/exec/exchange_staging_arena.cpp:248` throws `exchange staging arena exhausted: requested {} bytes ... (raise SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES)`; `nixl_transport.rs:720 rpc_request_lease(...)?` propagates the error out of the drain; `compute_node_service.rs:1302 handle_staging_lease` has no wait or retry. The arena's own destructor summary never printed because the CNs were force-exited.
324	
325	**Impact (inference, medium).** With the current FE plan the arena requirement for q03 grows as lineitem/N: ~SF1150 with `STAGING=16GiB`, or SF1000 with a 12 GiB arena, fails q03 after all the scan work is done. Broadcasting the small side (P3) would need < 1 GB of arena per CN for this family.
326	
327	**Proposed.** Short term: document `STAGING >= (N-1)/N x largest shuffled stream` in the cn-tuning guidance and fix P3. Engine: make `exchange_staging_arena::lease` block with a bounded wait on release instead of throwing, so a full arena throttles senders; or let the receiver push remote frames into pool memory on arrival (`push_packed` is already a deep copy) and release the lease immediately, keeping only the per-frame row count for `declare_input_cardinality`. Confidence high on the occupancy and the failure path.
328	
329	#### B7 (medium confidence, not adversarially verified). Per-task GPU_SCAN time rises 1.3-1.6x when four CNs scan concurrently, and at 1 CN the 4 pipeline slots bound the scan
330	
331	**Measured.** Per-task GPU_SCAN Computing (ms per ~2.2-2.3 GB task, `*-quent.json top_ops`): q03 lineitem 102 (1 CN) / 134-145 (4 CN) / 111 (standalone); q10 90 / 100-119 / 96; q12 orders 107 / 131-146 / 117; q14 151 / 240-249 / 176; q19 85 / 113-126 / 98; q07 130 / 179-186 / 142; q06 100 / 138-146. Per GB: q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q13 0.322 -> 0.498. q01 additionally shows 0.5-0.87 s stalls on 10% of splits on 2-3 of the 4 CNs, varying per run, with balanced bytes per CN (agent-notes/agg-only.md section 4); the 4-CN scan fragment is 1.43x (q01) / 1.6x (q06) the ideal quarter of the 1-CN fragment, which is 26-31% of the 4-CN wall. Aggregate read rates: q01 8.2 GB/s (1 CN) vs 22.9 GB/s (4 CN); q06 20.5 vs 50.8 GB/s, so the storage has headroom over what 4 slots pull. At 1 CN all 107 (q01) / 65 (q06) scan tasks are created within 9-50 ms and the 4 slots are busy 98%+ of the fragment wall (Queued median = half the wall); the memory gate does not bind for these two.
332	
333	**Cause not identified.** The `scan_split_read` probe recorded counts only in the digest because `quent_bp.py` reads the wrong attribute keys (`bytes`/`elapsed_ns` instead of `compressed_bytes`/`output_bytes`/`materialize_ns` emitted by `src/telemetry/scan_telemetry.cpp:52-56`), and even the raw probe covers read + decode together (`materialize_ns`). Candidates: GPFS client contention on concurrent O_DIRECT streams from 16 slots, host/GPU-side effects, NUMA placement. The CN launcher cannot raise `pipeline.num_threads` because `engine_settings.rs::derive_sirius_config_yaml` emits no pipeline block (and pairs with C3: 8 slots would request 156 GB in the cold-start wave).
334	
335	**Proposed.** Split the probe into read and decode, fix the digest keys (AGG-6), then A/B `SIRIUS_CN_USE_SIRIUS_DATASOURCE=false` and buffered reads / prefetch cache with the page cache warm vs dropped; add `SIRIUS_CN_PIPELINE_THREADS` to the derived config and sweep 6 and 8 on 1 CN with Quent on.

337	#### Disputed backpressure finding
338	
339	**BJ-6: "memory backpressure is absent for q03/q10/q12/q14/q19 at both 1 and 4 CN; the 6-15x over-reservation is harmless because concurrent reservations are far below the pool": refuted on the 1-CN half and on the mechanism; the conclusion (memory pressure is not this family's loss) stands.** Objection (data skeptic, agent-notes/refute-bj6): 4 concurrent tasks hold 58-80% of the 107.37 GB limit, not "far below"; the reservation gate blocked 47-178 ms per run in q10/q12/q14 at 1 CN in all three runs (see C3), 0 at 4 CNs and standalone; the engine pool's running peak reached 92-99% of the limit inside q03.r0 and q04.r0. "No arena exhaustion" is vacuous evidence because exhaustion is a hard failure, never backpressure (B6). The proposed regression guard is inverted: a tighter estimate reduces gating; guard instead that `num_threads x per-task cold-start request` stays well under the limit. Cost today is <= 0.18 s per query, so the impact ranking (planning, CN serialisation, scan contention dominate) survives.

343	`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/quent_bp.py:98-104` attributes staging leases by a +-0.5 s time window, so the last run of each query inherits the next cold run's first leases (cn4 q06.r2 shows 55 leases / 25.6 GB although q06 moves 64 bytes per stream; cn4-quent.txt per-fragment lease counts are likewise attributed by time, e.g. q07.r1's 1-task nation fragment shows 184 leases). 726	### 8.2 q21's emulated anti join over lineitem
727	
728	The translator lowers `RIGHT_ANTI_JOIN` to a right outer join plus `IS NULL` filter
729	(`node_translator.rs:1750, 1835-1842`) because the Substrait consumer lacks native anti joins
730	(P5 SAJ-5). In the fused q21 plan, `10: RIGHT ANTI` has the l3 lineitem scan on its build side and
731	`14: LEFT SEMI` has the l2 scan on its build side. DuckDB can flip both (`HasInverseJoinType` for
732	RIGHT, the SEMI arm above) but only if its estimates rank lineitem as the larger side against a
733	join output whose estimate is uncertain. If it does not flip, the engine builds a hash table on
734	~1-6B rows (12 B/row -> 73 GB for l2): OOM, bounded by fix 1. Standalone avoids the question with
735	`DELIM` joins from SQL (`standalone-failed/runs/q21.explain.txt`). Confidence medium; the P5
736	native-anti-join follow-up (item 5 in the report's section 4) removes the outer-join emulation
737	that inflates the intermediate 30x in q22 (`HASH_JOIN(15) in=6.59GB -> FILTER(16) 6.93GB ->
738	PROJECTION(17) 0.22GB`) and is the right fix if q21 disappoints.
